label: rem:h2o-bent-geometry
title: Bent geometry and the four hydrogen-bond directions
html:
Remark. Bent geometry and the four hydrogen-bond directions

Interpretation of the H_2O molecular braid.

Oxygen contributes two bonding sites and two lone pairs. In the assembly, the lone pairs occupy two of the four tetrahedral directions around oxygen as non-bonding phantom sites. This is the NH_3 \to H_2O extension of the methane T_d optimisation. Lone-pair repulsion relaxes the H–O–H angle from the ideal 109.5^\circ toward the observed \approx 104.5^\circ.

The four directions — two donor H and two acceptor lone pairs — provide the per-molecule input to the ice lattice. Each water molecule hydrogen-bonds to four neighbours, two as donor and two as acceptor. The resulting tetrahedral coordination tiles into hexagonal ice I_h (space group P6_3/mmc). The open tetrahedral network explains why ice is less dense than liquid water. The ice rule requires every bond to hold exactly one hydrogen. Which two of the four bonds carry this molecule's hydrogens is then the categorical origin of the Pauling residual entropy of ice, \approx R\ln(3/2). We develop the detailed tiling and its symmetry in the phase-symmetry model.
